notes: Old Reed (bible 5.14), keeper of Kestrel Lock; the toll board says gossip is accepted in lieu at his discretion (bible 7.2). Voice: dry, patient, unhurried. Tolls in gossip: a coin (reed.toll-paid) or a piece of gossip; both set the fact and gossip emits lock.gossip-paid for the lock's gameplay (follow-up bead). Rumour 17 is told through emit rumor.told. Class greetings only.

nodes.speaker: reed
nodes.text: A knight. Respectable. The barony's men came through this lock in my father's day, and they paid their toll in full. Gate's up and the board's there. Read it, and don't mind the flaking.

nodes.speaker: reed
nodes.text: Archer. Bow stays strung down, if you please. The herons on the sill have never been shot and they're the best gossips I've got. Read the board.

nodes.speaker: reed
nodes.text: Spells off the sill, thank you. Water goes where I tell it. The lock's been dredged, built, and rebuilt by better than you. Read the board.

nodes.speaker: reed
nodes.text: I count everything that passes this lock. Boats, coin, gossip. You I'm counting twice. Read the board, and don't read it as a menu.

nodes.speaker: reed
nodes.text: Kestrel Lock. Old Reed, keeper, forty years. There's a toll, there's a board, there's a kettle. Read the first, ignore the third.

nodes.speaker: reed
nodes.text: Back. Toll's the same. Gossip's gone up.

nodes.speaker: reed
nodes.text: Mind the sill. It's slippery. Everything here is.

nodes.speaker: reed
nodes.text: Stone barge, laden, two pennies. Empty, one. Silver barge, by imperial warrant. Pleasure craft, five. Gossip accepted in lieu at the keeper's discretion, and the keeper's discretion is generous. Well?

nodes.speaker: reed
nodes.text: Fair and square. Gate's open. Nobody pays in coin these days, so I'll remember you.

nodes.speaker: reed
nodes.text: A penny short, I see. Well, gossip's a legal tender here. Try that.

options.text: Seven beds have gone cold in Briar Glen.
The Gilded Tern pays double for crew who ask nothing.

nodes.speaker: reed
nodes.text: Seven beds. That'll do for tuppence, and I'll not repeat it. Pass, friend.

nodes.speaker: reed
nodes.text: The Tern. Aye, that's the one with the locked berth. Worth a penny and a half. We'll call it paid.

nodes.speaker: reed
nodes.text: No gossip. You'll find the river rather quiet, then. Come back with some.

nodes.speaker: reed
nodes.text: The barony dredged the Wend and built this lock halfway down, so the stone barges could get to the sea. It's older than me, and I've been at it forty years. The gates stick. So do I.

nodes.speaker: reed
nodes.text: Mags Oakum's Patient Ann, three times a week, laden. Lately a bit lower in the water than glenstone ought to sit. I've said nothing. It's none of my business, and I charge double for opinions.
